utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, do we only have two accused with us this morning?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are still waiting for another three -- another two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we're still waiting, I think, for the other three accused.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, another three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You may be seated. When the other accused come, they will be able to take their seats as well. So the accused may feel free to sit down. You can hear me now, I think. I said that you could sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated, Mr. Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Good morning to you all, ladies and gentlemen; good morning to the technical booth, the interpreters. I think they're all there. Good morning to the court reporters and legal assistants. Good morning, one and all. I think that after this pause that we've had we should bring us up to date, so shall we have the case called out, please, Madam Registrar, to begin with.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-30/1-T, the Prosecutor versus Kvocka, Kos, Radic, Zigic, and Prcac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Madam Hollis, could you introduce the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. The Prosecutor is represented by myself, Brenda Hollis, and Mr. Kapila Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Madam Hollis. The Defence, would you make yourselves known. Let's start with Mr. Krstan Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Krstan Simic, and Branko Lukic, with me, we both represent Mr. Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. As has been the case so far, the Defence team is complete, Ms. Jelena Nikolic, Mr. O'Sullivan, and myself. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. The Defence of Mr. Radic is represented by Toma Fila and Mr. Zoran Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Tosic is next.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. The Defence of Zoran Zigic is represented by me, Simo Tosic, attorney from Banja Luka, and I have Slobodan Stojanovic on my left, an attorney from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Jovan Simic. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Jovan Simic. Dusan Masic and Goran Rodic are on the team with me representing the Prcac defence case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Good morning to the accused. We are going to take up our proceedings where we left off. As you know, Judge Fouad Riad is unable to attend this morning because he is sitting on another case. Having had agreement from the two parties, the Defence and the Prosecution, we have decided, in agreement with Judge Fouad Riad, to carry on within the framework of Rule 71 and continue our hearing. We have taken this decision because we are always interested in expediency. As you know, the Trial Chamber has taken over this case under very difficult working conditions, but we have accepted to take on the case and so it is in all our interests to have a speedy and expeditious trial. As the parties agree, we are sitting under those conditions. I see that Mr. Tosic wished to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do apologise. Before we hear this witness today, if possible our defendant has asked to talk to us for a few minutes and discuss a few facts. So if that is possible, could you allow us five minutes to have a discussion before we go ahead? I don't know what he wishes to discuss but he has sent us a little note asking us to discuss certain facts before we hear the next witness, if the Court is in agreement. I do apologise for this but it is a matter that has just cropped up, and if possible we should be glad if you would accept our request. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this a personal encounter between you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That means that we have to interrupt the meeting, does it, leave the courtroom and come back afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I apologise, but perhaps our client and myself and Mr. Stojanovic could leave the courtroom for five minutes, have this discussion and then come back, not to waste the Court's time, if that is better in practical terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you know, Mr. Tosic, this upsets the trial considerably. You know that very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to know if this discussion could take place during the break. Mr. Tosic, what do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to respect the will of my client. If he considers that that will be a good time, I agree. If he feels that he needs to have this discussion before the break, then as his attorney I have to respect his will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tosic, would you please ask your client whether we could have this discussion during the break. You may leave your place to go and ask the client.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my client wishes to say that he wishes to revoke the power of attorney to engage us as his attorneys, myself and my colleague, and I should like to ask him to explain to the Trial Chamber his reasons for doing this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Hollis, what is your opinion in this matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, obviously an accused's right to have counsel is a paramount right; however, we don't believe it's an absolute right to fire your attorney in the midst of trial, especially when that attorney is an appointed counsel and not one that the accused has hired with his own funds. We believe that the Trial Chamber would have to be apprised of the reasons for this and then weigh those reasons very carefully, balancing the rights of the accused and the rights of all parties to continue within a speedy trial. So we don't believe it's an absolute right but we don't believe we can comment on the situation until the Trial Chamber has heard the reasons, and perhaps this will have to be done in camera with just Your Honours, the accused, and his counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then, I think that it is a good idea to give Mr. Tosic and Mr. Stojanovic an opportunity to have a meeting with Mr. Zigic, and in order to do that, I think that the accused should withdraw. Therefore, we're going to have a half an hour break; otherwise we're not going to be able to do all this. So let us have a half an hour break, after which we will reconvene to hear what the situation is. Witness, I do apologise for interrupting. I adjourn the hearing for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tosic, you have had an opportunity to have a meeting with your client. Where do we now stand?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my client wishes, in a closed session, with the presence of the Trial Chamber, the attorneys with him present, to state his reasons why he is firing me as his Defence attorney, the lead counsel. We discussed certain facts, that is to say, what we were not able to do, and that is one of the reasons that he is revoking his power of attorney. But at all events I should like my client to state his views regarding the circumstances, and then after he has said what he has to say, I would like to give you a report on what our duties have been and what we have done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tosic, the Chamber has nothing to do with the reasons that Mr. Zigic has for bringing into question you representing him. What we do know is that Mr. Zigic wishes to revoke the power of attorney and we have reached a decision on that matter, so you may be seated. The reasons for which Mr. Zigic is taking this step should be expounded to the Registry and not to the Trial Chamber. The three Judges of the Trial Chamber, and I say "three" because we had a meeting with Judge Fouad Riad, we conferred and discussed the matter with respect to Mr. Zigic's request with respect to his Defence counsel, neither the latter nor his co-counsel, Mr. Slobodan Stojanovic, that he does not wish to have them represent him further. Having studied the directives with respect to the appointment of Defence counsel, and bearing in mind the Statute of this Tribunal, especially Article 20 of the Statute, we arrived unanimously at the following conclusion: Mr. Zigic does have the right, if he wishes to do so, to table a request to the Registrar in order to seek a replacement for his legal counsel, the legal counsel which was appointed by the Registrar for his defence. He also enjoys the right, if he wishes to avail himself of that right, to table a written request so that he personally could secure his defence. From all this, it clearly emerges with respect to the appointment of Defence counsel the following -- and under these conditions it is not necessary for the Trial Chamber to hear the reasons for which Mr. Zigic would like Mr. Tosic and Mr. Stojanovic to cease representing him as his Defence counsel. The Trial Chamber would like to emphasise that these proceedings have to do with all the five accused, all of whom have the right to a fair and expeditious trial. The Trial Chamber therefore decides that we continue the trial until the end of the proceedings, until Wednesday, the 14th of June, which will be the last day, under the same conditions and representations, and until the Registrar has made a final ruling. In other words, what we're going to do is we're going to carry on with our work under the same conditions until such a time as the Registrar decides, makes a decision on the matter, and the request that Mr. Zigic will have to submit to the Registrar for consideration. That is the ruling of the Trial Chamber. Now I think we can continue with the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would call Witness Mirsad Alisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, please. Mr. Krstan Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting. We have a slight problem which will not upset the proceedings. After we heard Witness B, there was a mix-up that occurred with respect to the tendering of evidence linked to Witness B. The Prosecution withdrew its request and then I was not able to take the floor afterwards because our time was up for the day. But I should just like to state in relation to the testimony of Witness B, I would like to tender into evidence the fact that Witness B, when he identified the individuals, he failed to identify, recognise, Mr. Kvocka, but he did so in the courtroom. According to the documents that we tabled, this exhibit should be marked D27/1. The number is 21. Witness B did not recognise and identify Mr. Kvocka so we consider that this document should be tendered into evidence as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just be shown a copy of that just to verify what documents they're talking about. If the bailiff could perhaps assist. Your Honour, we would stipulate that the witness when shown a photo board identification failed to identify the accused Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I accept that, Your Honour, and we therefore withdraw our request, and I'm sure the Trial Chamber will take into account that fact when it comes to deliberate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are withdrawing that request; is that correct? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think that we can now proceed. I should like to remind you that tomorrow we have a Status Conference at 4.00 p.m., and maybe at the end of the morning I shall be able to tell you the agenda for that Status Conference so that you can prepare for it, because there are a series of questions that we have kept for the Status Conference and they will be discussed then. So that is tomorrow afternoon at 4.00, and at the end of tomorrow morning's work, I shall inform you of the agenda to be discussed. Let us now have the witness, who was already here once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're going to read the solemn declaration that the usher is going to hand to you, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. 7

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Do you feel comfortable, at ease?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for coming here. You are now going to be answering questions put to you by the Prosecutor. I give you the floor, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Waidyaratne:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please state your name.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: My name is Mirsad Alisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: The 19th of September, 1953.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you kindly state your place of birth.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I was born in Prijedor, Muharema Seljanovica, number 150.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Prijedor, which village? Could you describe the village?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: My village is called Raskovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the war, where did you reside?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I resided in Prijedor, Muharema Seljanovica, number 150.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that in Raskovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Raskovac, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your educational achievements?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I completed primary school and a secondary school for auto mechanics in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your occupation?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I was a car mechanic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you work?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I worked in the Tomasica mine as a dumper driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you start work?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I started on the 15th of March, 1975.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perform military service, compulsory military service?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In 1972/1973, in Zajecar, a town in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you attached to any unit, or did you specialise in any work?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: You mean in the army?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I was in the anti-tank missile unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you worked in the Tomasica mine as a dump driver from 1975.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the place called Ljubija mine?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Ljubija mines, Tomasica, Omarska, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until when did you work? When did you last -- or stop work?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I stopped worked on the 22nd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you stop work on the 22nd of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: In Tomasica, all the non-Serb population stopped working on the 22nd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody ask you not to come to work, or were you ordered not to come to work?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. My boss, Milorad Sipka, told me not to come to work. He was my immediate superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they give you a reason as to why they were stopping your work?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any others work during that period at the Ljubija mines?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. Just the people of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you stopped your work on the 22nd of May, 1992. Now, sir, I would draw your attention to the 30th of May, 1992. Do you recall that date?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I was in my own house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Raskovac.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: In Raskovac, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court what happened that day?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That day, at about 2.30, a uniformed soldier came, he was wearing the uniform of the Yugoslav People's Army, and he said that we should all leave our houses and go out into the street, which we all did; I, my wife, and our two children. When I went out onto the street, I saw a whole stream of people walking. Some people were carrying nothing; others were carrying a bag. Nobody knew where they were going. Whenever you asked them, they said they didn't know where they were going. We were just told to go to the auto market, which was the car market which was close by. When we came to this place where cars were sold, there were a lot of people standing there and we were ordered that children up to the age of 17 and elderly people over the age of 70 were to step to one side and that we should step to the other side. They separated us, and then buses began to arrive of the Autotransport Prijedor company, bus company, and first of all the women and children got into the bus. They were jammed packed and they would leave one by one. Afterwards, other buses came by and we were ordered to board the buses, which we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that there was a stream of people and the people were asked to proceed towards the open car market. Did you know these people and to which ethnicity they belonged?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I knew the people, they were my neighbours. They were of the Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that the buses came and that you were ordered to board the buses.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, or do you remember, how many people were in the bus that you were in?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: In my bus everybody had seats; they were sitting down. About 40 people, which is the number of seats that exist in a normal -- it was a normal public transport bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody escort the buses?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were two uniformed individuals. I knew both of them. One was called Acko, and the another one's surname was Turudija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bus that you were in, did it go to any place? Where did it go to?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: The bus started out. We were sitting down normally in the bus and we came to the marketplace, which is the entrance to the centre of Prijedor itself. I saw a lot of dead people on the pavement; there was a lot of blood. All the people that I saw and noticed were wearing civilian clothing. We were taken through Prijedor and we would encounter dead bodies. The bus then stopped outside the SUP building. It parked there and we stayed there for a time, and then we were ordered to continue. Once again we passed through the streets of Prijedor, and at the exit to Prijedor, the place is called Lukavica, which is where there was a bakery, and I saw a whole heap of people, dead bodies, wearing civilian clothing, of course. There was quite a lot of blood around there. We had to keep our heads bowed down, and then we went on towards Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what is the road that you refer to as Tomasica? Could you explain to the Court as to what this road is? Was it the normal road that proceeds to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: No. The road going to Omarska is the Prijedor-Banja Luka main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that buses proceeded. Were the buses stopped at any other places?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. The bus was stopped on the Zuti Put, the yellow road. I worked in Tomasica and I know this road very well. It was always referred to as the yellow road. The door was opened and we heard that they were going to take us out to slit our throats. One of the guards said, "There's no need to do that. We're taking them to Omarska and we'll get rid of them there." We were also stopped later on when we turned left onto the macadamised road surface, when we left the asphalt road, and I took the iron ore from Omarska to Tomasica there, so I know that road there. They told us to get out and they said that they would slit our throats. They cursed our balija mothers, our Turkish mothers, and so on. They used this derogatory form. When we came to Tomasica, I don't remember whether we were told to raise our heads, but I found my head raised and saw that everybody had looked up. The bus had already -- the bus in front of our bus had already been parked. We were ordered to step down from the bus six by six, with our hands up and behind our heads, like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I may interrupt. What was the destination? Where did the bus come to a stop? The final destination before you were asked what you saw, where six people were getting out of the bus.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That was Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been to Omarska before this?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Well, I went to Omarska frequently. I drove iron ore there and I took equipment there, and then I would drive trucks away with the iron ore from Tomasica. It was the same firm, actually, but with these two sections or departments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was during the time that you were employed in the Ljubija mines.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that the buses came and stopped at Omarska. What time of the day was it when these buses reached the camp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: It was towards evening. It was getting dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see around? Was there any light?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it? What was the light which was there at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Well, there were some lights at the hangar on the corner, reflecting light, and the workshop where the dumpers were repaired, there were big reflector lights there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the buses come and stop?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: The buses stopped between the hangar and the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I, Your Honour, at this stage introduce a new exhibit, a photograph of the model of the camp which could be given to the witness, marked as 3/90. Can I have the assistance of the usher. I have the provided the Defence and the Court with copies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please look at the exhibit that has just been provided to you. Could you indicate the place where the bus that you were in stopped.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: The bus was right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you take a pencil and mark it as "A1."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that there was another bus which was stopped in front of you, the bus that you were in.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was another bus in front of our own bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark that -- indicate that place as "A2? "

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw six people getting out of the bus with their hands on their heads.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you saw that from your place where you were seated in the bus. Where were you seated in the bus?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I was seated on the right side, in the window seat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see? Could you explain it to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: These six people came out with their hands raised up, as they were ordered to do. I saw some guards whom I knew from before. And this guy who was named Predojevic fired a burst of fire and killed these six people, and he told them, "Fuck your balija mothers. You know where you have come and you know what's in store for you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned a person by the name of Predojevic. Did you see him at that instance? How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He was dressed in a summer uniform of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he armed with?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He had an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other guards around the place or any other persons from the camp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: There was some other guards there, not very many of them. I did not know them, so I don't know who.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see what happened to the people who got down from the bus, the six persons who got down from the bus, after Predojevic shot?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: After I got down from the bus, I could see them lying down on the ground in front of the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see -- what did Predojevic do after that? Did you observe him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: No. He just stood there. He was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned the name of Predojevic. Did you know this person before the war, before this instant?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know him, and how did you know the name?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I used to drive trucks and lorries, and once I took some wood to Slobodan Savic, who also worked at the Tomasica mine, and Predojevic was also there and he was helping us, so that's how I got to meet him. So I know from then that his surname is Predojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this person by the name of Predojevic in the camp during your detention thereafter?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I'd see him at Omarska. He was a guard at Omarska, and I would often see him at the pista.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a regular guard? And what time did he -- do you know what time he worked or what shift he worked in?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Predojevic worked in Radic's shift. They worked 12 hours per shift, from 7.00 to 7.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will take you back to the time that you saw this shooting. After the shooting, were you ordered out of the bus?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were going out of the bus, six by six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you all asked to go?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: We were told then to go to the administration building, actually, in front of the administration building, at the entrance of the administration building. That's where we were stopped and we had to put our hands on the walls of the administration building, with three fingers pointing towards the wall. There, we were inspected and they took our money, our valuables, our watches, our chains, what things they could find. And they also took down our particulars, the surnames, the names, the dates of birth, the addresses of the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I introduce a diagram of the administration building, which has already been marked as 3/77A. With the assistance of the usher to give to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please see the diagram. You said earlier in your testimony that you were asked to line up in front of the administration building at the entrance. Could you show and indicate the place where you were asked to stand when you were searched.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Right there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark that place as "A3."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you said, sir, that you were searched and your information were taken down. During that time, could you kindly say as to who searched you and whether you saw any guards or soldiers around that place?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I only knew Paspalj and Popovic of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them there at that instance?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The persons you named as Paspalj and Popovic, did you know them before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know them?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Well, as I said, I was driving these trucks from Tomasica to Omarska and I used this tank truck to spray the road, hose the road with water, along these lines. So I worked in Tomasica and I saw them there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them thereafter in the camp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When and where? Could you say as to when and where, and in which shift they worked?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I saw Paspalj and Popovic because I spent a lot of time on the pista, and they were in Radic's shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you earlier also mentioned a person by the name of Radic. Do you know the full name of this person by the name of Radic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Mladic -- Mladen Radic, known as Krkan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him or did you have -- had you known him before the war, before your detention in the camp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He was a policeman in Ljubija and that's how I knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you spoken to him? Have you seen him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you see Radic in the camp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I would see Radic at the beginning of the shift and at the end of his shift. Sometimes I would also see him at Omarska camp, but that was not frequent during his shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were searched and your information was taken by the guards, were you ordered to go to any place in the building?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you ordered to go?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: We were ordered to this room which was later dubbed Mujo's room. It is this way, through this corridor, and then the door to the right and then into this Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the diagram that you have, there is a number marked in all of those places. Could you kindly refer to the number in that room.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Here, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it? What is the number which is there in that diagram?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you also kindly show, indicate, from the entrance as to how you went to that room which is marked as A9.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel is kindly asked to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: This hall, straight down this hall to this door, which was on the right side and which led into this room, number A9. This is where I entered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now this room which is marked as A9, did you refer to it by a name, or how did you all refer to that room?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That room was called, it was given the name, Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why it was called Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: One Mujo was in this room, and then when something was needed to communicate with the guards, something was to be done for the guards -- for the prisoners with the guards, he was the one who communicated with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went into Mujo's room, did you see anybody, and what was the condition of the room?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: When I came into Mujo's room, I could see the whole of Prijedor in Mujo's room because I knew all of the people in that room. Whenever I turned I saw familiar faces. Nobody spoke, nobody said a thing; they were all silent. They were all lost and had this expression of being lost on their face. Nobody said anything; nobody had any comment to make.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnicity were these people; do you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Most of them were of the Muslim ethnicity but there were some Croats among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you spend the night, the first night that you spent in the camp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I spent this first night in the lavatory or in the toilet, which was part of Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you spend the night in the lavatory in Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Because there was no room in Mujo's room, there was no space. It was cramped. There were many people there in addition to myself, in the lavatory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using that Exhibit 3/77, could you kindly show the place or the lavatory that you testified to.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: This is where the lavatory was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark that place as "L."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, I apologise for interrupting but we have here "A3" indicated by the witness and another A3 which is part of the composition of the sketch. Perhaps you could explain the A3 that the witness marked, which was located between A15 and A16, because as you can see, there's another A3 where the "L" is. But I think that if you explain this it will be clear, that the "A3" marked by the witness is located between A15 and A16 already inscribed on the diagram and the exhibit, and that he has now placed the letter "L" right next to the A3 already marked on the diagram. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. The A3 which the witness marked between A15 and A16 was the place where they were searched and where their information was taken. And the "A3" which is in the diagram, is in there which has been marked before that. The letter "L" which the witness has just indicated was to show that was the place of the lavatory, or the toilet; the first night that he spent. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you spent the first night in the lavatory in Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you spend in Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to any other place in the morning?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: In the morning, we heard an order given out to the people who came in the night before into Mujo's room, they were told to step outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come out of the room?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anybody there at that instance?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I saw Miroslav Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Miroslav Kvocka was wearing a camouflage police uniform with a blue beret.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything at that instance?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He said that we should walk slowly, that we shouldn't go fast. If anybody made a quick movement of any kind, that he personally would kill him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he armed at that instance?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, Miroslav Kvocka had a pump-action rifle on his right shoulder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you all ordered to go to?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I was ordered to go to the pista.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court as to what this place that you refer to as "the pista" is, using the exhibit number 3/90.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I have the assistance of the usher to help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, please look at that exhibit, and could you show the place that you refer to as "the pista."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That's the pista here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you observe there? Did you see anything else there in that place?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: When we came here, there were people on the pista already there, straight at the beginning. They were all civilians, and I saw that they had been beaten the previous night because they were covered in blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any guards present at that place at that instance?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: They were standing around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the pista, were you ordered to sit down?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the pista, did you observe that day a vehicle coming to that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. A TAM 2000 truck known as Zuco came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour was it?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: It was yellow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see the truck leaving the pista?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it loaded with anything before it left?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: On the truck there was a machine-gun with ammunition, and that machine-gun was unloaded and the ammunition on the roof of the administration building, and it was -- a soldier was positioned there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the truck leaving at that instance?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it loaded with anything before it left?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That truck parked here and they loaded up the dead bodies of people onto the truck. There was a patch of grass here beside the "white house." But they loaded it up with dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who loaded the bodies onto the truck?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: The guards working in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody else, any camp leaders present at that instance when the bodies were loaded onto the truck?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was Miroslav Kvocka there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he doing there?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He was there. He was present there. He took us out onto the pista. He was standing there; that's where he was, next to the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned about the person by the name of Kvocka. Did you know this Miroslav Kvocka before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know him? Could you explain to the Court as to how you knew him before the war.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Well, Kvocka is married to the Crnalic lady who also lived in my street, and also before the war he worked as a policeman; that's how I knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen Kvocka before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any other members of the family to whom he was married?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew his father-in-law and his mother-in-law and the brothers of his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the pista, were you able to observe around and see as to what -- could you state to the Court what you saw around when you were detained on the pista.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: While we were on the pista, we could see everything, the guards who were there and who was coming, the comings and goings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the conditions during that period?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Well, they were bad. We were out on the asphalt. Sometimes we were ordered to lie down on our stomachs, and this would take place and we would have to lie like that for hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you provided with water and food?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Rarely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were detained on the pista, during the nights were you ordered to go to any other place?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you state what these places were.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: To the restaurant, which was within the frameworks of the administration building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time were you ordered to go to the restaurant, generally?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: In the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you spent the night in the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Not every night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during a night that you spent in the restaurant, did you see a shooting take place?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you approximately or roughly say when this incident took place?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Well, it was at the beginning, when I arrived, when we arrived. There was an elderly man; he was about 70 years old and his name was Nasic. And we were ordered to go to the restaurant. We got up, because there were hundreds of us on the pista. And the machine-gun on the roof, the one standing there, he shot with that machine-gun above our heads. And Nasic did not dare go into the restaurant. The other prisoners tried to coax him into going into the restaurant because he said that -- they said that if you didn't obey orders other people would suffer. So finally, he entered the restaurant. We were ordered to sit down but Nasic remained standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you see Nasic in the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I have the Exhibit 3/77A be given to the witness too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the diagram. Could you first show or indicate the place that you call the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That's it here. That's the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that diagram, could you say what the letter and the numbers which are indicated there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, using that diagram, could you kindly show the place that you saw Nasic while you were in the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I saw Nasic here, next to the line where the food was distributed. That's where Nasic was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you kindly mark that place with the letter "N."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you kindly show and indicate the place that you were that night.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I was located in this corner here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark that place as "M."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you said that you saw Nasic in the restaurant. Could you explain to the Court what happened thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: While Nasic was standing, he said that it was unbearable, that we couldn't -- he couldn't take it any more, that those of us who had been persecuted couldn't take it any more. But we saw -- I saw at the end of the restaurant, that is to say, outside here, I saw a guard. I saw Plavsic and he was called Cvitan. He had a white lock of hair and he was referred to by the other guards as Cvitan as well. I saw standing next to that guard Miroslav Kvocka; he stood right next to the guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say what happened when Nasic was standing and-- when he was standing.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: The guard shot a burst of gunfire and he killed Nasic straight away. He fell down. There were cries and screams, and there were other people who were wounded. Afterwards, Kvocka came up right to this corner where I was standing and he said, "Why don't you make him keep quiet? Why didn't you stop him from saying what he said?" And afterwards the three young men who had been wounded were taken out. I didn't see them dead or alive after that. I don't know where they went, where they were taken. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what happened to Nasic? Did you see Nasic thereafter in the camp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, using the diagram again, could you kindly indicate the place where you saw Plavsic when he shot Nasic, and mark that place with the letter "P."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you saw Kvocka and subsequently he came and stood -- the first time that you saw Kvocka, will you mark that place with the letter "K1."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Subsequently, you said that the person by the name of Kvocka came and said why the detainees didn't keep Nasic quiet. Could you indicate that place as "K2," where you saw Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is this the same person that you referred to as Kvocka -- earlier in your testimony you referred to a person whom you saw when you came out of Mujo's room and named him as Kvocka. Is this the same person that you saw that night?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He was wearing a camouflage police uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned a person by the name -- the guard named Plavsic. Could you describe to the Court as to what he looked like.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He was a little shorter than me, a little fatter than me. He had curly hair and he had a white strand of hair here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know in which shift or during what time he worked, in whose shift he worked?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Plavsic was also in Krkan's shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the name of the guard prior to you coming to the camp, the name of Plavsic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get to know the name?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I just heard the guards calling out to each other. I heard them saying the name and I remembered it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. During your detention in the pista, did you see any persons being beaten?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know a person by the name of Hrnic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know him, and could you explain to the Court as to what he --

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Well, I knew Hrnic. He drove trucks. He was a rich young man. We would meet in Asaf's cafe, Muhamed Izetic, in his pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you associate with him before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Well, we weren't actually friends but we did know each other, and in fact very frequently we would meet each other in cafes. We would see each other around, although we weren't actually bosom buddies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you see this person during your detention in the camp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning -- that is to say, he was beaten up rather a lot. He was taken in front of the administration building, he was told to place his hands against the wall of the administration building, and they beat him. They beat him a lot, and it's amazing what Hrnic was able to take during the times that he was beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you see him being beaten?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it? Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: It was in front of the administration building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the persons who beat him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the guards. They would take turns in beating him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these persons who beat him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I recognised Paspalj, Popovic, Predojevic. They beat him most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately when was this, when you saw this beating?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: It was during the first week after my arrival in the camp. He was brought there in the morning. They would beat him for half an hour, take him off, bring him back, beat him again for another half an hour, take him away again and bring him back again, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him with injuries? Did you see Hrnic with injuries?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. When Hrnic was going to lunch -- we were told to run to lunch but he wasn't able to run. You could see that he was dragging his leg and that he was making grimaces from the pain, that it was painful for him to walk and that he couldn't actually run. And when he went into the restaurant he would be hit with a rifle butt in the back, on his head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During these beatings, did you see any camp leaders or people in authority present?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: No. I don't remember, actually. I don't remember having seen them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, during your detention in the pista, could you kindly tell us how long you spent in the pista out of the total time that you were detained?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I spent 46 days on the pista.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the pista, did you see another detainee being shot?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw Mehmed Alisic killed on the pista.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This person whom you referred to as Mehmed Alisic, did you know him before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know as to what ethnicity he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court as to what you saw with regard to the incident concerning Mehmed Alisic.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: At one point when I happened to look up, we were lying down on the pista, on the asphalt there, I saw Mehmed standing, and at the same time, further off I saw a guard with a rifle held up like this, in the air. I was surprised to see Mehmed standing because we were all ordered to lie down. And then he shot a burst of gunfire. I saw Mehmed fall; his head was down on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see -- did you know this guard before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe how he looked and how he was dressed at that instance.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He was wearing the olive-green/grey uniform of the Yugoslav People's Army. He was tall, strongly built, bald.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him prior to this, present in the camp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him around in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see what happened to Mehmed Alisic? Was his body removed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: His body was removed, and I didn't see him after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see where they took this body -- took his body?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, now I would draw your attention to an incident that you saw in the camp concerning a person by the name of Gordan Kardumovic. Did you know a person by the name of Gordan Kardumovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were friends. We visited each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which ethnicity group he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how he was employed before the war, what his employment was?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He worked at the petrol station, and then he opened a cafe of his own by the Mladen Stojanovic School in Prijedor. The cafe worked well; because I visited the cafe and I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Gordan while you were detained in the camp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you state as to when you saw him first and where you saw him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I saw Gogi for the first time in front of Mujo's room. There's a door there. Not the door that we go in and out of, but by a tap. There was some taps for washing there. The miners working in Omarska used to wash their boots there and so on. We were allowed to go there from time to time to wash a bit, and that's where I met Gogi for the first time in Omarska, in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he speak to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did speak to each other. I asked him how come he was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you ask that question from him? Was there any reason?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Well, I asked Gogi Kardum how come he was there because as I say we were friends, we saw each other, but I didn't know what ethnic group he belonged to actually. And then he told me on that occasion, "I am a Croat."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall which time period that you saw him for the first time in the camp; during which month it was?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: It was round about the end of June and the beginning of July. He had come from Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him thereafter?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I saw Gogi Kardum dead on the grass after that. That was the first and last time after that first occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see his body, and what did you see?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That night, I spent the night in the hangar. I don't know the number of the room. But in the morning we were to go out to see to our ablutions, and as soon as we left the hangar there's a door and you go directly onto the grass from there. And when I got there I saw that there were dead people around, and unfortunately I stood right by where Kardum was. I recognised him. He was covered in blood. And that's how it was. The guards said that we had to urinate there, and I found this difficult because Gogi Kardum was there, right by me, but I had to do what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I, Your Honour, use Exhibit 3/90, for the witness to be able to show these places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, looking at the photograph, could you show the place that you saw the body of Gogi, or Gordan Kardumovic.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark that place or indicate that place with the letter "G."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you close enough to see his dead body and to observe the injuries?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I was right next to Gogi Kardum, right by his legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I seek your permission to introduce a photograph which the accused -- which the witness brought and handed over to the Prosecution. We were unable to get the copies for the Defence but I have given notice to the Defence. I would produce this, and as the witness wants the original back, may I, at the conclusion of the testimony, the proceedings, I will get a copy and retrieve this original from the Court. May I have the permission to produce this. And I would mark this as -- this is a new exhibit, 3/91.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, please look at the photograph and could you explain to the Court as to who the persons who are seen in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: This is Gogi Kardum and that's me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you kindly tell the Court as to when this photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That photograph was taken a little before the war. In 1990, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it taken?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That photograph was taken next to a restaurant which was called Sevdah, and we would eat lamb on a spit. We would picnic there. We would play football. Muslims, Croats, Serbs, we would all go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this photograph was in your possession until you gave it to me, until you gave it to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, after your detention in the pista, were you at any time transferred to, or had the opportunity to go to any other place, any other building?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Well, we were beaten up in the "white house," in the hangar, in the restaurant, and in Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your detention, were you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Not beaten up. Transported. The interpreter apologises. We were transported to the "white house," and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were released from the camp, were you again taken to Mujo's room?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that? What was the period?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: It was during the day and in the evening as well, depending. Sometimes you would go to Mujo's room during the daytime; sometimes you would be taken there at night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in Mujo's room, during the latter part of your detention, did you see a person by the name of Zgog?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I saw him in Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were together on the pista as well, Zgog and I.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know this person before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the ethnicity of this person?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He was an Albanian, a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he before the war? Did you know where he was employed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Zgogi was a football player, he played football in the Second Federal League. Later on, before the war, he worked as a coach.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in Mujo's room, did you see an incident involving Zgog?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe what happened and when this took place.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: One day, during the daytime, Paspalj came into Mujo's room, and Popovic came in after him. They called Zgog out and they said, "Come here, coach." That's how they referred to him. He came up and Paspalj said that he should collect up 500 Deutschemarks within the space of 15 minutes, otherwise he'd be killed. He beat Zgog with his baton and left and said he would be back in 15 minutes. Zgog collected up the money. He asked the prisoners for money but they didn't have any money themselves. I don't know from where, but money was put forward, and when Paspalj came in, Zgog was able to hand him over the money. Paspalj counted out the money and he set a certain sum aside and put it in his pocket. Then he continued to count the money, and then he cursed Zgog's mother and he said that he needed to -- that there wasn't 500 Deutschemarks there and that he needed another 200, and then began to beat him. He beat him all the time. There were two columns in Mujo's room, concrete pillars. He left the room. Zgog broke the window that was above me, I was underneath the window, and he took a piece of glass and wanted to slit his own throat -- started slitting his throat with that piece of glass fragment. Mehmed Besic was there and took hold of his arm and prevented him from slitting his own throat, as he intended to do. In the meantime, Paspalj and Popovic came in. The room was full, but at that moment it was empty. The centre of the room was empty. We were all around the walls of the room and he started beating Zgog. He beat him and beat him with anything that came to hand. Popovic was with him, of course, and joined in. They told us that we should all leave Mujo's room that day, on that occasion, when Paspalj was beating him, and we did all leave the room. They called our names out, perhaps 200 names, and I was amongst those 200 and so was Bajram Zgog. They transferred us to the hangar, on the ground floor of the hangar, and that's when the prisoners were brought there for the first time. There was barbed wire all around it, there was a lot of mud, and otherwise that was a workshop for the heavy duty mining vehicles. And I saw Bajram Zgog there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Bajram Zgog after that incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. We left together, where we were transferred to. Zgog Bajram tried to hide. You couldn't really hide but he did what he could to stop the guard from seeing him; he would sort of bend down. But later on I was transferred from the hangar to Mujo's room and I didn't see Bajram Zgog any more after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May this be a suitable time to stop, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Mr. Waidyaratne. It is noon and we're going to have a half an hour recess. So we'll pause for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Mr. Waidyaratne, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before the recess you were referring to an incident where you described the assault or the beating of a person by the name of Bajram Zgog. Do you remember the time, or the period, that this incident happened?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: It was somewhere around July, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the latter part of July?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: It was the first half of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, before we get to a new area, I would ask you a question. You testified with regard to the incident concerning the shooting of Mehmed Alisic. You said that the guard who fired -- whom you saw firing at Alisic was bald. Could you describe what you meant by "bald"? What sort of hair, or could you describe what you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He had a receding hairline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Also, when you testified about Miroslav Kvocka, you said that he was dressed in a police camouflage uniform. Could you describe as to what colour?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: It is camouflage, which is to say multicoloured, but basically blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, I would take you to a different area. The time that you spent in Mujo's room in the latter part of your detention, did you see a person by the name of Dzevad Grozdanic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: I saw Dzevad within the frameworks of Mujo's room, so to speak. But there are some concrete troughs there, and that's where I saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know this person before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know as to what he was -- as to how he was employed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He was a haulier; he had a truck. But before the war he lived in Switzerland. But he is from Poharska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him in the camp in Mujo's room, did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him. He was all beaten up. Dzevad was in no condition to talk to anyone. You could see traces of beating and bruises on his head and all over his body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain more as to what these -- you say that he was beaten up and you saw bruises. Could you explain what these injuries were that you could see?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: He had bruises on his face and he was covered in blood. Also on his chest, there were cuts on his chest as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him thereafter?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know to which ethnic group he belonged?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw him, you said that there were some concrete -- could you say as to which place this is in Mujo's room.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That was in front of the lavatory, in front of the lavatory in this hall, and you pass by these troughs to enter the lavatory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it inside the lavatory?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: It was part of the lavatory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, during your detention in the camp, were you separately or individually beaten?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the date or the month that this took place?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: That was on the 4th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You specially remember this date. Is there any reason you remember specifically the date?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the day -- the birthday of my youngest son. That is why I remember that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you that day before this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: On that day I was on the pista.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe what happened then?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD ALISIC
utterances.text: The guard who was on duty in the Omarska camp, he beckoned me with his finger to approach him. So I did, and he ordered me to stand against the wall of the administration building, with my hands and normally the three fingers leaning against the wall. He told me to wait there, and then he went to the "white house" to get some other people. Predojevic and Paspalj were there. Predojevic came up to me and I told him, "Do not make an invalid out of me. You don't need to do that." Predojevic said, "What do you mean a disabled person? We're going to kill you now." So I froze, my blood ran cold. This person who came, then he told me to come inside. So I climbed up on the first floor, and there is a sort of a widening on the landing. Near the landing on the first floor there were some more guards waiting there. They told them to get some whips. These were special whips, they had lead balls on the top, attached to them. And I buttoned up my jacket to mitigate the blows for a while. Then they ordered me to take off my jacket, which I did, and also my T-shirt. Predojevic said, "Look at the dog and kill him." So they starting beating me up, and I was there actually bellowing like an ox. I was in excruciating pain, and I cried out because of pain; hoping that somebody could hear me. There were some people in the other offices. There was Miroslav Kvocka, Radic was there.
